sun.brief: THE SUN (Light island, cell id 931). An island off the bottom of the tree, centre (0, 112). Its roads: an inner ring of radius about 6.5 (road nodes 522-528) round the Light start figure (fixed, in the middle), an outer ring of radius 13 (road nodes 529-548, every 18 degrees), and four spokes (straight roads) along the axes; the spoke going UP (towards -y) leads to the rest of the tree. Region: everything within radius about 18.5 of (0, 112), except near the up-going spoke above the outer ring, where other pieces of the tree sit (see neighbours). Art direction, the director's own words: 'Light should be simple, just do light rays going out'. Make it read as a sun: radiance outwards, calm and clear, built on the island's circles. Images: img-sun.png.

moon.budget: about 55-75 nodes, of which 6-10 in the side circle
moon.brief: THE MOON (Darkness island, cell id 933). An island off the top of the tree. Its roads form a crescent: an outer arc of radius 19 round (0, -109) (road nodes 590-610 roughly, tips 590 and 591 at the top) and an inner arc of radius about 15.9 round (0, -117.3) (road nodes 611-623 roughly); the crescent's hollow (towards -y, inside the inner arc) is open space. The Darkness start figure (fixed) sits at (0, -95.7) on a road from 617 down to 601. Roads leave sideways from 608 and 599 and down from 601 to 440 (440 is the end of another region; a neighbour figure hangs there). The island also owns a small separate road circle far away at about (107.8, -24.9), radius about 7.6 (road nodes 625-636): put a small moon-related figure in it too (inside that circle, hung from its road nodes). Region: the crescent band between the two arcs, the hollow inside the inner arc (up to about radius 14 round (0, -117.3)), a margin of about 3 outside the outer arc, and the side circle's inside. Art direction, the director's own words: 'the moon should have these celeste mystical curves you know'. Celestial, mystical, curved. Images: img-moon.png (the crescent) and img-moonside.png (the side circle).

thunder.brief: THUNDER (Thunder island, cell id 932). An island at the left of the tree, centre (-103.665, -33.683). Its roads: the Thunder start figure (fixed) in the middle inside a small pentagon of road nodes (551-562), a pentagonal web of road cells round it (road nodes 553-577), an outer arc on the left (west) side (road nodes 578-586) closing two outer cells, and the open east side, where a road leaves from 570 through 588 to the tree. Region: inside the web cells and the two outer cells between the web and the outer arc, plus a margin of about 3 beyond the web on the open east side (keep clear of the road 570-588). Art direction, the director's own words: 'and lightning, I'm not so sure how'. Your call: storm, lightning, thunder in a way that still follows the style rules (no straight spikes; zigzags are acceptable only if they read as designed, built on a rhythm). Images: img-thunder.png.

chaos.budget: about 80-120 nodes in all, spread over the five cells
chaos.brief: CHAOS (the hub at the centre of the whole tree; cell ids 79 wood, 80 earth, 81 metal, 82 water, 83 fire). Five lands surround it; land axes (th in the polar form): fire 0, earth 72, metal 144, water 216, wood 288. The hub's roads: an inner ring of radius 4.2 round the Chaos start figure (fixed, at the origin), an outer ring of radius 14.5, and five straight spokes from the inner to the outer ring along the borders between lands (th = 36, 108, 180, 252, 324), each with a middle road node at radius about 9.35. The five hub cells are the five wedges between the spokes, between the two rings; each piece must lie inside one wedge (polygons in the data) and is listed under that wedge's cell id. Beyond the outer ring are the lands (other pieces, see neighbours): stay inside radius 14.5. A curve may cross a spoke only at its middle road node or at a ring node, split into two pieces there (rule 5). Art direction, the director's own words: 'For chaos it should be swirls into the center'. Swirling, turning, drawn in towards the centre; the hub should read as one figure across the five wedges (rotating one wedge's design by 72 degrees is fine, P(r, th) makes that easy). Images: img-chaos.png.
